name: Basis

subjectOf.text: No uncollateralized algorithmic stable cryptocurrency, such as Basis or NuBits, had produced a provably stable mechanism for its tokens as of the time of writing.
subjectOf.abstract: At the time of this writing no uncollateralized algorithmic project had created a provable stable mechanism for its tokens.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396522

subjectOf.text: As of the time of writing, no uncollateralized algorithmic stable cryptocurrency project had produced a provably stable mechanism for its tokens.

subjectOf.text: Distributing newly minted coins to shareholders, as Basis planned, is exploitable: shareholders can collude to hold their new money and drive the price up, which triggers further minting that benefits the colluders.
subjectOf.abstract: However, it is possible the shareholders would collude to drive the price up by holding their new money
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies - First Order Principles (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3402701
scope_conditions: new supply distributed to an identifiable shareholder group

subjectOf.text: A Basis-style bond scheme succeeds only while demand for the currency grows at a sufficient rate; the authors' simulations show it fails when demand is stagnant at equilibrium.
subjectOf.abstract: According to our simulations, this scheme will succeed as long as demand for the currency is growing at a sufficient rate, but it will fail if the demand is stagnant at equilibrium
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies - First Order Principles (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3402701
